newsitem.title: USA: Two firms in semiconductor sector plan job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Two firms in semiconductor sector plan job cuts.

text.p: Semiconductor industry firms Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Varian Associates Inc. announced plans Thursday to trim their payrolls due to slower demand for computer chips.
Advanced Micro, which makes computer chips, said it planned to cut up to 200 jobs and take a $6 million charge and semiconductor equipment firm Varian said it was cutting 115 workers.
"In light of weak demand, the company has carefully reviewed operations in order to achieve and maintain appropriate staffing levels," Advanced Micro said in a statement.

"Issues that were identified as a result of those reviews included overlapping or redundant activities and skill sets that do not match current or future requirements. These concerns are being addressed by the workforce reduction."

Advanced Micro reported a $35 million loss in the second quarter ended June 30 vs. a profit of $80.7 million in the year-ago quarter, reflecting a significant decline in revenues from its once-lucrative flash memory chips.
Sunnyvale, Calif.-based Advanced Micro employs 12,500 people worldwide.
Varian said its cuts, which reduce overall employment by less than 2 percent, affect semiconductor equipment factories in Gloucester, Mass. and Palo Alto, Calif.

"The semiconductor industry continues to suffer from overcapacity and price discounting, and that inevitably means lower demand for new chip-making equipment," said Executive Vice President Richard Aurelio. "While we know the cycle will turn up again, right now it's impossible to predict when.
"As a result, these moves are needed to keep our costs in balance with the slowdown in orders during the interim."
He said about 85 of the positions affected are at the Gloucester plant, which had a similar reduction in mid-August. The remainder are at the Palo Alto unit.
Semiconductor sales have slowed considerably this year, reflecting a glut in the market and sharply lower prices for memory chips. In recent weeks, however, prices have started to rebound.

Spot prices for 16 megabit DRAM chips, the most popular configuration, have risen to $10 from $8 in early August. The increase benefits all producers, including Micron Technology Inc. and Texas Instruments Inc., he said.
Advanced Micro's stock fell 87.5 cents to $15.125, and Palo Alto, Calif.-based Varian was down 62.5 cents at $47.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
